name: A-level Chemistry (AQA 7405)

selected_options.practical_endorsement: not covered (teacher-assessed, separate from the grade)

material_vintage: AQA AS and A-level Chemistry (7404/7405) specification, Version 1.2 (July 2026), linked from aqa.org.uk/7405 and itemised on 2026-09-27: every content code at its deepest level (3.1.1.1-3.3.16), the mathematical requirements MS 0.0-4.3, the practical skills PS1.1-4.1, the apparatus and techniques ATa-l and the twelve required practicals. The hands-on apparatus list (practical endorsement only) is declared out of scope. Assessment: Paper 1 (2 h, 105 marks, 35%: physical chemistry 3.1.1-3.1.4, 3.1.6-3.1.8 and 3.1.10-3.1.12, and inorganic chemistry), Paper 2 (2 h, 105 marks, 35%: physical chemistry 3.1.2-3.1.6 and 3.1.9, and organic chemistry), Paper 3 (2 h, 90 marks, 30%: any content; 40 marks on practical techniques and data analysis, 20 marks across the specification, 30 multiple-choice). Stage tests and the mock are original questions in AQA's style; every numerical answer was computed when the course was built.
level_source: RQF Level 3 (GCE A-level), per Ofqual's register listing for AQA 7405

learner_notices.text: The A-level grade comes only from the written papers. AQA also reports a separate practical endorsement, assessed by a teacher watching you work in a lab. This course teaches the required practicals' methods, observations, analysis and evaluation for the written papers, but it cannot award or replace the endorsement.

Chemistry answers often need drawn structures and curly-arrow mechanisms. In this course they are described in words and text formulae; in the exam you must draw them, so practise sketching each mechanism on paper as you go.
